summary: Environment provisioning fails: org tag stripping causes assume-role/session-tag denial during ops onboarding
description:
Issue summary: During scheduled ops onboarding (analytics pipeline access), the bootstrap job that assumes cross-account roles fails with AccessDenied. Impact: SRE and Platform engineers cannot complete onboarding for the analytics sandbox; several CI jobs blocked.
High-level root cause suspected: resource-level permission boundary/organization tag normalization striping critical session tags required for role assumption.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Pipeline runs assume-role to analytics-ops-prod AWS account using central-assumer role
3) STS AssumeRole returns 403/AccessDenied with message referencing missing required session tags or principal
4) Deployment fails when deploy-runner attempts to create service-account in GKE staging
observed_behavior: STS AssumeRole failed with AccessDenied: "Missing required session tag: department"
Cloud IAM audit logs show request with no session tags after our token broker exchanges
GCP workload identity mapping failed with 'Principal not found' due to missing tag-based condition
expected_behavior: AssumeRole should succeed with session tags forwarded, role creation completes, and onboarding pipeline finishes
Token broker should preserve session tags and comply with organization's condition keys
logs: AWS STS error (CloudTrail): EventID=abcd-1234 - AssumeRole - ErrorCode=AccessDenied - ErrorMessage='Failed due to missing session tag: env' - 2026-03-11T10:21:33Z
GCP IAM audit: policy denied principal binding - 2026-03-11T10:22:01Z - httpRequest: {...} (see cloud logging link)
comments: Support (Aisha Romero) 2026-03-11: Initial triage - reproduced with onboarding pipeline; gathering CloudTrail and WIF logs. Noting similar symptoms to INT-582173 (session-name/tag truncation).

SRE (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-12: Observed org policy that enforces 'aws:PrincipalTag/department' and denies if tag missing. The token broker appears to be dropping tags when exchanging to staging SA. Investigating token broker codepath.

IAM (Lina Chen) 2026-03-12: Confirmed that permission boundary applied to 'central-assumer' role is configured to drop certain ec2:ResourceTag keys during cross-account assumes. Asking for sample AssumeRole request ID.
Support (Aisha Romero) 2026-03-12: Attached CloudTrail request IDs and a snapshot of the broker's STS payload. Opening a short-lived workaround to bypass tag requirement for onboarding.

Platform Eng (Marcus Lee) 2026-03-13: Implemented temporary allowlist PR in infra (see related_github_prs) and performed test run; onboarding succeeded for one job. Need to coordinate org-policy change for permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Token broker does not forward session tags due to an encoding mismatch in the STS AssumeRole call; reproduced locally by invoking broker with long session name.
Hypothesis 2: Org policy tag-normalizer step strips tags on cross-account assume for roles created before policy rollout.
Evidence: CloudTrail shows the original request contains tags, but subsequent AssumeRole call made by broker lacks the tag header.
Temporary workaround validated: add explicit condition exception for the 'analytics/onboard' role in org policy (PR merged: infra#5734).
resolution: Temporary fix: added an allowlist exception in org policy for the analytics onboarding role and patched the token broker to propagate session tags for short runs. Long-term: schedule org policy audit + patch to token broker to preserve session tags even after encoding/length normalization. Follow-up action: open INT-100902 to coordinate policy remediation and runbook update.
